//! Ownership locks the database's sidecar; stat pins its inode. `serve.lock` is only an address hint.
use std::{fs::{self, File}, io::{Read, Seek, SeekFrom, Write}, path::{Path, PathBuf}, time::Duration};
use snapback4_core::{Engine, RuntimeError, Store};
#[cfg(unix)]
use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt;

pub(crate) struct Owner {
    _sidecar: std::sync::Arc<File>,
    identity: (u64, u64),
    path: PathBuf,
    record: Option<File>,
    reclaimed: Option<String>,
    pub(crate) token_authority: Option<crate::serve::token::Authority>,
}

/// The address `doctor` dials for the server that owns this store: the
/// published loopback address itself, or, for a wildcard bind, that family's
/// loopback on the same port. A published non-loopback address is not followed.
pub(crate) fn inspector_address(store: &Path) -> Option<std::net::SocketAddr> {
    let path = store.canonicalize().ok()?;
    dialable(&address(&path)?)
}

fn dialable(published: &str) -> Option<std::net::SocketAddr> {
    use std::net::{IpAddr, Ipv4Addr, Ipv6Addr, SocketAddr};
    let address = published.strip_prefix("http://")?.parse::<SocketAddr>().ok()?;
    let ip = match address.ip() {
        ip if ip.is_loopback() => ip,
        IpAddr::V4(ip) if ip.is_unspecified() => IpAddr::V4(Ipv4Addr::LOCALHOST),
        IpAddr::V6(ip) if ip.is_unspecified() => IpAddr::V6(Ipv6Addr::LOCALHOST),
        _ => return None,
    };
    (address.port() != 0).then(|| SocketAddr::new(ip, address.port()))
}

fn resolve(store: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
    match store.canonicalize() {
        Ok(path) => Ok(path),
        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
            let parent = store.parent().filter(|p| !p.as_os_str().is_empty()).unwrap_or(Path::new("."));
            snapback4_core::private_fs::directory(parent).map_err(|e| failure(store, e))?;
            Ok(parent.canonicalize().map_err(|e| failure(store, e))?.join(store.file_name().ok_or("store path has no filename")?))
        }
        Err(e) => Err(failure(store, e)),
    }
}

fn failure(path: &Path, reason: impl std::fmt::Display) -> String {
    format!("E_STORE at {}: {reason}; restore a regular store/address file and retry", path.display())
}

#[cfg(unix)]
fn same_file(a: &fs::Metadata, b: &fs::Metadata) -> bool { a.dev() == b.dev() && a.ino() == b.ino() }

#[cfg(unix)]
fn regular(path: &Path, create: bool, database: &Path) -> Result<File, String> {
    snapback4_core::private_fs::auxiliary_file(database, path, create, 128)
        .map_err(|e| failure(path, e))
}

// @ref LLP 3000.019#3.4 — sidecar flocks fence backend writers and share device ownership without locking SQLite.
pub(crate) fn command(store: &Path) -> Result<Owner, String> { acquire(store, false, Duration::ZERO) }
pub(crate) fn device(store: &Path) -> Result<Owner, String> { acquire(store, true, Duration::ZERO) }
// @ref LLP 3000.009#5.3 — a restarting host waits for watchdogs to finish group cleanup.
pub(crate) fn host(store: &Path) -> Result<Owner, String> { acquire(store, false, Duration::from_secs(5)) }

#[cfg(unix)]
fn acquire(store: &Path, shared: bool, wait: Duration) -> Result<Owner, String> {
    let deadline = std::time::Instant::now() + wait;
    for _ in 0..16 {
        let path = resolve(store)?;
        snapback4_core::private_fs::directory(path.parent().ok_or("store path has no parent")?)
            .map_err(|e| failure(&path, e))?;
        // Stat before opening either auxiliary file; a refused probe creates
        // no database. Only the sidecar lock grants permission to create one.
        let before = snapback4_core::private_fs::database_metadata(&path).map_err(|e| failure(&path, e))?;
        let sidecar = snapback4_core::private_fs::owner_file(&path)
            .map_err(|e| failure(&snapback4_core::private_fs::owner_path(&path), e))?;
        let mut cleanup = None;
        loop {
            let locked = if shared { sidecar.try_lock_shared() } else { sidecar.try_lock() };
            match locked {
                Ok(()) => break,
                Err(fs::TryLockError::WouldBlock) if std::time::Instant::now() < deadline && *cleanup.get_or_insert_with(|| stopped_host(&path)) => std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(25)),
                Err(fs::TryLockError::WouldBlock) => return Err(busy(&path)),
                Err(fs::TryLockError::Error(error)) => return Err(failure(&path, error)),
            }
        }
        if !snapback4_core::private_fs::owner_is_named(&path, &sidecar) { continue; }
        snapback4_core::private_fs::database_file(&path).map_err(|e| failure(&path, e))?;
        let database = snapback4_core::private_fs::database_metadata(&path).map_err(|e| failure(&path, e))?
            .ok_or_else(|| failure(&path, "database disappeared during ownership acquisition"))?;
        if before.as_ref().is_some_and(|old| !same_file(old, &database)) { continue; }
        let mut reclaimed = None;
        let record = if shared { None } else {
            let record_path = path.with_file_name("serve.lock");
            if let Some(pid)=owner_pid(&path) {
                if unsafe {libc::kill(pid as libc::pid_t,0)} == -1 && std::io::Error::last_os_error().raw_os_error()==Some(libc::ESRCH) {
                    reclaimed = Some(format!("reclaimed stale serve.lock: dead PID {pid}; directory {}", path.parent().unwrap().display()));
                }
            }
            let file = regular(&record_path, true, &path)?;
            file.set_len(0).map_err(|e| failure(&record_path, e))?;
            Some(file)
        };
        return Ok(Owner { _sidecar: std::sync::Arc::new(sidecar), identity: (database.dev(), database.ino()), path, record, reclaimed, token_authority: None });
    }
    Err(failure(store, "database path kept changing during ownership acquisition"))
}

#[cfg(not(unix))]
fn acquire(store: &Path, _: bool, _: Duration) -> Result<Owner, String> { Err(failure(store, "database ownership requires Unix")) }

fn stopped_host(path: &Path) -> bool {
    // A CLI owner or a host not yet announced still refuses immediately. A
    // reachable listener does too; only a prior host's cleanup gets a wait.
    // This is a refusal/wait hint, never permission to open the store: the
    // sidecar must still be acquired. Never dial a non-loopback address hint.
    address(path).is_some_and(|published| dialable(&published).is_none_or(|address|
        std::net::TcpStream::connect_timeout(&address, Duration::from_millis(50)).is_err()))
}

pub(crate) fn busy(path: &Path) -> String {
    let owner = address(path).map(|address| match owner_pid(path) { Some(pid) => format!("{address} (pid {pid})"), None => address })
        .unwrap_or_else(|| "another CLI command or a server starting up (address pending)".into());
    format!("E_STORE_BUSY at {}: this store is live; owned by {owner}; directory {}; no work was admitted. Stop its `snapback4 dev` or `snapback4 serve` process (or wait for the owning CLI command), rerun this command once, then restart the server. Exclusion holds while <database>-owner is left in place; deleting or replacing it while a process runs ends exclusion and does not stop that process", path.display(),path.parent().unwrap_or(Path::new(".")).display())
}

#[cfg(unix)]
pub(crate) fn address(path: &Path) -> Option<String> {
    // A missing/replaced address record cannot grant ownership. Never follow
    // a symlink (including one to the database), nor block on a FIFO.
    let record = path.with_file_name("serve.lock");
    let file = regular(&record, false, path).ok()?;
    let mut text = String::new();
    file.take(1024).read_to_string(&mut text).ok()?;
    let mut lines = text.lines();
    let port = lines.next().and_then(|s| s.parse::<u16>().ok());
    lines.next().map(str::to_owned).or_else(|| port.map(|p| format!("http://127.0.0.1:{p}")))
}

/// The owning host's PID from its address record (`pid N` on the third line).
#[cfg(unix)]
fn owner_pid(path: &Path) -> Option<u32> {
    let record = path.with_file_name("serve.lock");
    let file = regular(&record, false, path).ok()?;
    let mut text = String::new();
    file.take(1024).read_to_string(&mut text).ok()?;
    text.lines().nth(2)?.strip_prefix("pid ")?.parse().ok()
}

#[cfg(not(unix))]
fn owner_pid(_: &Path) -> Option<u32> { None }

#[cfg(not(unix))]
pub(crate) fn address(_: &Path) -> Option<String> { None }

impl Owner {
    pub(crate) fn report_reclaim(&self, verbose: bool) {
        if verbose && let Some(note) = &self.reclaimed { eprintln!("note: {note}"); }
    }

    // @ref LLP 3000.000.000#11-wave-11-factual-release-narration — unlink only our address inode; the ownership sidecar remains named.
    pub(crate) fn clear_address(&self) {
        #[cfg(unix)]
        if let Some(file) = &self.record {
            let path = self.path.with_file_name("serve.lock");
            if let (Ok(held), Ok(named)) = (file.metadata(), fs::symlink_metadata(&path))
                && same_file(&held, &named) {
                let _ = fs::remove_file(path);
            }
        }
    }
    pub(crate) fn worker_lock(&self) -> std::sync::Arc<File> { self._sidecar.clone() }

    pub(crate) fn path(&self) -> Result<&Path, RuntimeError> {
        #[cfg(unix)]
        {
            let meta = snapback4_core::private_fs::database_metadata(&self.path)
                .map_err(|e| RuntimeError::Store(failure(&self.path, e)))?;
            if meta.is_some_and(|m| (m.dev(), m.ino()) == self.identity) { return Ok(&self.path); }
        }
        Err(RuntimeError::Store(failure(&self.path, "owned database moved or was replaced; stop and reopen its current path")))
    }

    pub(crate) fn open_store(&self, timeout: Duration) -> Result<Store, RuntimeError> {
        let mut store = Store::open_with_busy_timeout(self.path()?, timeout)?;
        #[cfg(unix)]
        store.retain_ownership(self._sidecar.clone())?;
        Ok(store)
    }

    pub(crate) fn open_engine(&self, bound: &snapback4_lang::Bound, timeout: Duration, now: i64) -> Result<Engine, RuntimeError> {
        let store = self.open_store(timeout)?;
        if store.meta("release")?.is_some() {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Generation("this store belongs to a deployment; use `deploy` to activate source and `serve` to run it".into()));
        }
        Engine::new_at(store, bound.schema.clone(), bound.programs.iter().map(|p| p.program.clone()), now)
    }
}

impl Drop for Owner { fn drop(&mut self) { self.clear_address(); } }

pub(crate) fn announce(owner: &mut Owner, address: std::net::SocketAddr) -> Result<(), String> {
    // @ref LLP 3000.019#3.4 — live token work runs through the owner, with proof of local store access.
    owner.token_authority = Some(crate::serve::token::publish(owner.path().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?)
        .map_err(|e| failure(&owner.path, e))?);
    let file = owner.record.as_mut().ok_or("device ownership has no server address record")?;
    file.set_len(0).and_then(|_| file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(0))).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    // First-line port is retained for the dev inspector; the third line names the owning process.
    write!(file, "{}\nhttp://{address}\npid {}\n", address.port(), std::process::id()).map_err(|e| e.to_string())
}

fn previous_frontend(dir: &std::path::Path, web: bool) -> Option<Option<&'static str>> {
    super::proof_advice::frontend_template(dir, web).filter(|(version,_)| matches!(*version,"0.4.28"|"0.4.29"|"0.4.30"|"0.4.31")).map(|(_,template)|template)
}

/// Adapt adds missing proof infrastructure, preserving files and script names
/// already owned by the application. It never runs a package manager.
pub(super) fn plan(dir: &std::path::Path, own: &super::OwnSchema, enable_day2: bool) -> std::io::Result<Vec<(&'static str, String)>> {
    let web = dir.join("src/App.tsx").is_file();
    let router = dir.join("app/_layout.tsx").is_file();
    if !web && !dir.join("App.tsx").is_file() && !router { return Ok(Vec::new()); }
    let shape = super::starter::Shape { title: super::title(dir), password: own.identity.is_some_and(|(p, g)| p && !g),
        personas: own.identity.is_none().then(|| own.personas.clone()).filter(|p| !p.is_empty()),
        body: super::starter::Body::Home(None), offline: own.offline.clone() };
    let path = dir.join("package.json");
    let text = std::fs::read_to_string(&path)?;
    let mut package: Value = serde_json::from_str(&text).map_err(std::io::Error::other)?;
    let router = router && !web && package["main"] == "expo-router/entry";
    if !web && !dir.join("App.tsx").is_file() && !router { return Ok(Vec::new()); }
    let original = package.clone();
    let day2_text = std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("scripts/day2-proof.mjs")).ok();
    let referenced_day2 = package["scripts"].as_object().is_some_and(|scripts| scripts.values().any(|v| v.as_str().is_some_and(|s| s.contains("scripts/day2-proof.mjs"))));
    let missing_managed_day2 = day2_text.is_none() && matches!(package["scripts"]["day2:proof"].as_str(),
        Some("node scripts/day2-proof.mjs" | "node scripts/day2-proof.mjs versions/v1.q versions/v2.q" | "node scripts/day2-proof.mjs versions/v1 versions/v2"));
    let managed_day2 = day2_text.as_deref().is_some_and(super::proof_advice::known_day2) || missing_managed_day2;
    let day2 = enable_day2 || referenced_day2 || package.pointer("/snapback4/starter/day2") != Some(&json!(false)) && managed_day2;
    // Deleting both the command and file records a durable opt-out on apply.
    // Preview/check never write the inferred choice. Explicit --day2 opts in again.
    if (package["snapback4"].is_null() || package["snapback4"].is_object()) && (package["snapback4"]["starter"].is_null() || package["snapback4"]["starter"].is_object()) {
        package["snapback4"]["starter"]["day2"] = json!(day2);
    }
    let backend = package["scripts"]["backend"].as_str().and_then(|s| s.strip_prefix("snapback4 dev --port ")).and_then(|s| s.parse::<u16>().ok())
.or_else(|| launcher_port(dir, "backend")).unwrap_or(4400);
    let frontend = launcher_port(dir, "frontend").or_else(|| package["scripts"][if web { "dev" } else { "start" }].as_str()
        .and_then(|s| s.split_once("--port ")).and_then(|(_, rest)| rest.split_whitespace().next()).and_then(|n| n.parse::<u16>().ok())
        .or_else(|| std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("vite.config.mts")).ok().and_then(|s| s.split_once("server: { port: ").and_then(|(_, rest)| rest.split(|c: char| !c.is_ascii_digit()).next()).and_then(|n| n.parse::<u16>().ok())))
        ).unwrap_or(if backend != 4400 { backend.saturating_add(1) } else if web { 5173 } else { 8081 });
    let mut generated = vec![("package.json", pretty(&package))];
    let mut flags = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();
    if router { flags.insert("template".into(), "social".into()); }
    if day2 { flags.insert("day2".into(), String::new()); }
    files(&mut generated, &Options { positionals: vec![dir.to_string_lossy().into_owned()], flags, json: false }, backend, frontend, web, &shape);
    // A saved version is immutable application evidence. Never fill its missing
    // fixture files from today's working release during an adaptation.
    generated.retain(|(name, _)| !name.starts_with("versions/") || {
        let version = name.split('/').nth(1).unwrap();
        !dir.join("versions").join(version).exists()
    });
    // New directories capture the current source and contemporary fixtures. Flat
    // legacy snapshots remain untouched evidence; they are never propagated.
    // Custom proofs own their saved source layout; do not manufacture snapshots.
    if !managed_day2 && !enable_day2 { generated.retain(|(name,_)| !name.starts_with("versions/")); }
    let wanted: Value = serde_json::from_str(&generated[0].1).unwrap();
    for group in ["scripts", "devDependencies"] {
        if !package[group].is_object() { package[group] = json!({}); }
        for (key, value) in wanted[group].as_object().unwrap() {
            let old = package[group].get(key).and_then(Value::as_str);
            let managed = group == "scripts" && old.is_some_and(|old| match key.as_str() {
                "day2:proof" => managed_day2 && matches!(old, "node scripts/day2-proof.mjs" | "node scripts/day2-proof.mjs versions/v1.q versions/v2.q"),
                "backend" => old.strip_prefix("snapback4 dev --port ").is_some_and(|n| n.parse::<u16>().is_ok()),
                "dev" | "preview" => old.strip_prefix(if key == "dev" { "vite --port " } else { "vite preview --port " }).and_then(|s| s.strip_suffix(" --strictPort")).is_some_and(|n| n.parse::<u16>().is_ok()),
                "start" | "web" => old.strip_prefix(if key == "start" { "expo start --port " } else { "expo start --web --port " }).is_some_and(|n| n.parse::<u16>().is_ok()),
                _ => false,
            });
            if managed || ((key == "day2:proof" && enable_day2 || key == "frontend:proof" && super::proof_advice::known_frontend(dir) || key == "playwright-core" && (super::proof_advice::known_frontend(dir) || super::proof_advice::referenced(dir, "scripts/frontend-proof.mjs"))) && old.is_none()) { package[group][key] = value.clone(); }
        }
    }
    let mut config_changes = Vec::new();
    if web {
        if let Ok(current) = std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("vite.config.mts")) {
            // Replace only the exact initializer forms, allowing their port literals.
            let numbers = current.split("port: ").skip(1).filter_map(|s| s.split(|c: char| !c.is_ascii_digit()).next()?.parse::<u16>().ok()).collect::<Vec<_>>();
            let mut normalized = current.clone();
            for number in &numbers { normalized = normalized.replace(&format!("port: {number}"), "port: 5173"); }
            let reference = include_str!("starter/web/vite.config.mts").replace("port: 4173", "port: 5173");
            if normalized == reference { config_changes.push(("vite.config.mts", runtime_vite(&current, backend, numbers.first().copied().unwrap_or(5173)))); }
        }
    }
    let inherited_frontend = previous_frontend(dir, web);
    if let Some(template) = inherited_frontend {
        if let Some((_, text)) = generated.iter_mut().find(|(name, _)| *name == "scripts/frontend-proof.mjs") {
            *text = frontend_proof(include_str!("frontend-proof.mjs"), template, web);
        }
    }
    let referenced_after = |path: &str| package["scripts"].as_object().is_some_and(|scripts| scripts.values().any(|v|v.as_str().is_some_and(|s|s.contains(path))));
    let mut additions: Vec<_> = generated.into_iter().skip(1)
        .filter(|(name, _)| {
            if *name == "scripts/frontend-proof.mjs" { return inherited_frontend.is_some() || !dir.join(name).exists() && referenced_after(name); }
            if *name == "scripts/day2-proof.mjs" { return day2 && (managed_day2 || !dir.join(name).exists() && (enable_day2 || referenced_day2)); }
            if !dir.join(name).exists() {
                return name.starts_with("versions/") || referenced_after(name);
            }
            false
        }).collect();
    additions.extend(config_changes);
    if package != original { additions.push(("package.json", pretty(&package))); }
    Ok(additions)
}

fn launcher_port(dir: &std::path::Path, name: &str) -> Option<u16> {
    let text = std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("scripts/launch.mjs")).ok()?;
    // Recognize the generated fallback expression, not client application code.
    let marker = if name == "backend" { "low === null ? " } else { ": low === null ? " };
    text.split_once(marker)?.1.split_whitespace().next()?.parse().ok()
}

## 1. Contract

Implementer: PROOF workstream, 2026-10-14. Wave 11 fix list 1 authorizes
one published `snapback4/proof` Node module. It owns orchestration, never client
custody or backend/bundler supervision in the product. Existing `startDev(args)`
and `stopChild(child | {url, stop})` recipes remain usable as module exports.

`startDev`, `startServe(directory)`, `startStatic(directory)` and
`startVite(directory)` return `{url, pid, logs, stop}`. Options carry cwd,
environment, arguments and bounded ready/stop deadlines. Read PORT_LO/PORT_HI
at invocation: absent means an OS-assigned port; exactly one set refuses. With
both set, validate 1 <= LO <= HI <= 65535 and bind the first free port in that
inclusive range; exhaustion refuses. Qualification's occupied first port must
be skipped, never adopted. The existing native SNAPBACK4_READY line already names its direct child PID (LLP 3000.011.004.000); no new readiness log is needed. The listening process binds first and keeps that socket;
never adopt an already-serving port. Vite uses its supported JavaScript server
API in a directly spawned Node child, strict ports, the project's config and
a per-launch identity middleware. The directly spawned frontend calls its
server listen API for each candidate; no probe-and-release step exists. With
no range it calls listen on port 0, which the tested Vite API supports with
strictPort; it reads the actual retained socket address. Static hosting uses a directly spawned Node
child with traversal protection, correct wasm MIME and SPA fallback.

All child stdout/stderr go to separate files beneath `logs/`. Read complete
lines from those files, strip ANSI, bound readiness, and reject premature exit.
Native ready lines must name the directly spawned PID. To assert HTTP identity,
the kit sets a random SNAPBACK4_PROOF_ID only in the child environment;
`/auth/config` includes `proof_id` only when this variable is nonempty. It
confers no authority or bypass, and ordinary servers omit it. Both static and Vite frontend child
responses carry an `x-snapback4-proof` marker. Identity validation
precedes returning a handle. No public development door is enabled in serve.

Register every spawned child and browser process for an exit-time SIGKILL
sweep, using retained native ChildProcess handles, not process-name kills.
TERM followed by bounded KILL/reap stops a child. Every cleanup action has
its own bound and later actions still run when an earlier action fails.
`cli(args)` runs the native binary, awaits close, returns separate stdout and
stderr, and has a command deadline. It never runs npm/npx or shell strings.

`withBrowser({executablePath: process.env.CHROME}, callback)` launches Chromium
through playwright-core, closes with a bound, and registers its actual browser
process. Root needs --no-sandbox; other hosts first attempt a sandboxed launch
and retry without it only on recognized sandbox-unavailable diagnostics: "No usable sandbox", "Running as
root without --no-sandbox", "Failed to move to new namespace", "SUID sandbox",
"sandbox ... Operation not permitted", or "Failed to unshare ... Operation not
permitted". Unrelated failures never retry.
`waitForFresh` polls for nonempty changed text; `fillRN` clears and types real
keystrokes; `statusText` uses text selectors; `selectByValue` selects stable
option values. The browser executable is CHROME (when provided), undefined executablePath is omitted from launch options, then Playwright's
installed Chromium is used; an absent executable refuses at launch, with its path.
waitForFresh defaults to 30 seconds. Binary resolution is resolveBinary from
the same installed snapback4 package (override SNAPBACK4_BIN only for explicit
workspace tests); the opt-in identity requires CLI/client 0.4.28 or newer and
an older CLI omits proof_id and therefore fails the exact marker assertion; no inferred version comparison or success claim is made. cli(args) does not
invoke package managers; publication uses its existing guarded command runner.

None interprets an HTTP acknowledgement as rendered settlement.

## 2. Explicit source and aliases

`deploy dir --schema file` compiles exactly that saved Quarry file and stages

regardless of the saved file's name. Compile diagnostics name the selected input.

The snapshot is RAII-owned and removed on success or error; nothing is executed

write selected-schema types there. Package prepared signatures and native bytes

dependency paths against the original native crate's directory. TOML parsing

in a fixture argument escapes any value, including an exact bare alias name. This affects only fixture case argument substitution, not protocol decoding.

   352	pub(super) fn advance(request: Request, shared: &Shared, body: &str) {
   353	    if !shared.personas { return respond(request, 403, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&crate::dev_clock::release())})); }
   354	    let payload = match serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(body) {
   355	        Ok(payload) => payload,
   356	        Err(_) => return respond(request, 400, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&crate::dev_clock::input("clock advance takes {\"duration\":\"+2m\"}"))})),
   357	    };
   358	    let each_boundary = match payload.get("eachBoundary") {
   359	        None => false,
   360	        Some(serde_json::Value::Bool(value)) => *value,
   361	        Some(_) => return respond(request, 400, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&crate::dev_clock::input("eachBoundary must be a boolean"))})),
   362	    };
   363	    let duration = payload.get("duration").and_then(|value| value.as_str());
   364	    let milliseconds = match duration.ok_or_else(|| crate::dev_clock::input("clock advance takes {\"duration\":\"+2m\"}"))
   365	        .and_then(crate::dev_clock::duration) {
   366	        Ok(milliseconds) => milliseconds,
   367	        Err(error) => return respond(request, 400, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&error)})),
   368	    };
   369	    // Serialize clock callers only. Background slices check advancing after
   370	    // engine admission and skip during this synchronous drain.
   371	    let advance = lock(&shared.maintenance).advance.clone();
   372	    let _advance = lock(&advance);
   373	    let _advancing = Advancing(shared);
   374	    // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.12 — simulated time makes retries due without stealing a live worker's claim or viewer session.
   375	    let advanced = (|| {
   376	        // Match claims' engine-then-clock lock order: no claim can land
   377	        // between shifting its lease and publishing the advanced clock.
   378	        let mut engine = lock(&shared.engine);
   379	        let before = crate::dev_clock_store::saved_boundaries(&engine);
   380	        shared.dev_authority(&engine)?;
   381	        let mut clock = lock(&shared.clock);
   382	        let mut next = clock.clone();
   383	        let now = next.advance(milliseconds)?.max(shared.time_audience_clock.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Acquire));
   384	        let boundaries = crate::dev_clock_store::crossed_boundaries(&engine, &before, now, shared.hold_schedules)?;
   385	        lock(&shared.maintenance).advancing = true;
   386	        engine.advance_worker_leases_at(milliseconds, clock.now()).map_err(|e| e.refusal())?;
   387	        *clock = next;
   388	        let offset = now - snapback4_core::now_ms();
   389	        let isolated = if crate::dev_clock_store::has_data(&engine) {
   390	            format!("; use {} for isolated time tests; clock advance --port N targets its printed port (guide jobs)", crate::dev_clock::isolated_command())
   391	        } else { String::new() };
   392	        let message = format!("cumulative offset {offset:+}ms (authoritative floor included); process offset lasts until restart{isolated}");
   393	        Ok((now, offset, message, before, boundaries))
   394	    })();
   395	    let (now, offset, message, before, boundaries) = match advanced {
   396	        Ok(result) => result,
   397	        Err(error) => return respond(request, 400, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&error)})),
   398	    };
   399	    // @ref LLP 3000#contended-read-serving — a developer is awaiting this
   400	    // request; synchronous clock-advance work intentionally keeps request QoS.
   401	    let drained = (|| {
   402	        let mut crossed = Vec::new();
   403	        if each_boundary {
   404	            for (index, at) in boundaries {
   405	                crossed.extend(engine_work(shared, |engine, _| engine.fire_schedule_boundary_at(now, index, at))?);
   406	            }
   407	        }
   408	        let mut work = work(shared, true, 0)?;
   409	        work.schedules += crossed.len();
   410	        work.fired.extend(crossed);
   411	        Ok::<_, RuntimeError>(work)
   412	    })();
   413	    match drained.map_err(|error| error.refusal()).and_then(|work| completed_drain(work, crate::lifecycle::stopping())) {
   414	        Ok(work) => {
   415	            let schedules = crate::dev_clock_store::schedule_report(&lock(&shared.engine), &before, &work.fired, now, shared.hold_schedules, each_boundary);
   416	            respond(request, 200, json!({"now":now, "advancedMs":milliseconds, "offsetMs":offset, "skewMs":offset, "eachBoundary":each_boundary, "message":message, "work":work, "schedules":schedules}))
   417	        }
   418	        // Time remains advanced if maintenance fails; callers must not
   419	        // retry the advance blindly. The normal tick retries pending work.
   420	        Err(error) => respond(request, 500, json!({"now":now, "advancedMs":milliseconds, "offsetMs":offset, "skewMs":offset, "eachBoundary":each_boundary, "message":message, "denied":refusal_json(&error)})),
   421	    }
   422	}

   424	/// `POST /dev/jobs/<job>` with `{"args":{..}}`: queue one run of a job as the
   425	/// system on the dev clock and drive chunks until it is done or parked. This is
   426	/// what `snapback4 run <job>` forwards to while dev owns the store.
   427	pub(super) fn run_job(request: Request, shared: &Shared, name: &str, body: &str) {
   428	    use snapback4_core::{JobState, error::Refusal, ir::ProgramKind, wire};
   429	    let service_route=request.url().starts_with("/jobs/");
   430	    let service=if service_route {
   431	        match super::session_identity::principal_of(&request,shared) {
   432	            Ok((principal,kind,snapback4_core::identity::SessionScope::Full)) if kind=="service" && principal.starts_with("service:") => Some(principal),
   433	            _ => return respond(request,403,json!({"denied":refusal_json(&Refusal::new("E_AUTH","auth","triggering a deployed system job requires a full service token").guide("jobs"))})),
   434	        }
   435	    } else {
   436	        if !shared.personas {return respond(request,403,json!({"denied":refusal_json(&Refusal::new("E_AUTH","auth","/dev/jobs is a development door; use run <job> --release <dir> with a service token").guide("jobs"))}));}
   437	        None
   438	    };
   439	    let refuse = |request, status, refusal: Refusal| respond(request, status, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&refusal.guide("jobs"))}));
   440	    let payload: serde_json::Value = match serde_json::from_str(if body.trim().is_empty() { "{}" } else { body }) {
   441	        Ok(payload) => payload,
   442	        Err(error) => return refuse(request, 400, Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", format!("the request body is not JSON: {error}; send {{\"args\":{{..}}}}"))),
   443	    };
   444	    if service_route && !shared.personas {crate::release_requests::Scope::admit(&shared.release_requests,||*lock(&shared.generation));}
   445	    let program = lock(&shared.bound).programs.iter().find(|p| p.program.name == name).map(|p| p.program.clone());
   446	    let program = match program {
   447	        Some(program) if program.kind == ProgramKind::Job => program,
   448	        Some(other) => return refuse(request, 404, Refusal::new("E_OP", "op", format!("{name} is a {}, not a job; queries are POST /q/<op>, mutations POST /m/<op>", other.kind.word()))),
   449	        None => return respond(request, 404, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&super::dev_doors::stale(shared, Refusal::new("E_OP", "op", format!("unknown job {name}")).guide("jobs")))})),
   450	    };
   451	    if let Some(raw)=payload.get("args") && let Some(why)=super::dev_doors::persona_argument(shared,&program.args,raw) {return refuse(request,400,why);}
   452	    let mut args = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();
   453	    if let Some(fields) = payload.get("args").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_object) {
   454	        for (field, value) in fields {
   455	            let Some(kind) = program.args.get(field) else { return refuse(request, 400, Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", format!("{name} takes no argument {field}"))); };
   456	            match wire::from_json(kind, value) {
   457	                Ok(typed) => { args.insert(field.clone(), typed); }
   458	                Err(why) => return refuse(request, 400, Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", format!("argument {field}: {why}"))),
   459	            }
   460	        }
   461	    }
   462	    let mut admitted=lock(&shared.engine);
   463	    crate::release_requests::stamp(admitted.generation());
   464	    if !service_route && let Err(why) = shared.dev_authority(&admitted) { drop(admitted); return refuse(request,403,why); }
   465	    if let Some(service)=&service {
   466	        if let Err(why)=super::session_identity::mutation_authority(&request,shared,&admitted,service) {drop(admitted);return refuse(request,403,why);}
   467	    }
   468	    let queued=admitted.enqueue_job(name,args,shared.now());
   469	    drop(admitted);
   470	    crate::release_requests::executed();
   471	    let id = match queued {
   472	        Ok(id) => id,
   473	        Err(error) => return respond(request, 400, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&error.refusal())})),
   474	    };
   475	    // FIFO: earlier queued runs finish first, as with `run` on a stopped store;
   476	    // the background tick may run some chunks too, through the same engine.
   477	    let run = loop {
   478	        let current = {let engine=lock(&shared.engine);crate::release_requests::stamp(engine.generation());engine.job(&id)};
   479	        match current {
   480	            Ok(Some(run)) if matches!(run.state, JobState::Done | JobState::Parked) || crate::lifecycle::stopping() => break run,
   481	            Ok(Some(_)) => {}
   482	            Ok(None) => return respond(request, 500, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&RuntimeError::Store(format!("job {id} vanished")).refusal())})),
   483	            Err(error) => return respond(request, 500, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&error.refusal())})),
   484	        }
   485	        let (chunk, logs) = engine_work(shared, |engine, budget| (engine.run_job_chunk_for(shared.now(), budget), engine.take_native_logs()));
   486	        for line in logs { snapback4_core::diagnostic!("snapback4: native {line}"); }
   487	        match chunk {
   488	            Ok(Some(chunk)) if chunk.state == JobState::Parked && shared.personas => shared.refusals.job(&chunk),
   489	            Ok(_) => {}
   490	            Err(error) => return respond(request, 500, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&error.refusal())})),
   491	        }
   492	    };
   493	    snapback4_core::diagnostic!("snapback4: job {} {} on request: {} chunk{}, {} row{} written", run.name, if run.state == JobState::Done { "done" } else { "parked" },
   494	        run.chunks, if run.chunks == 1 { "" } else { "s" }, run.rows_written, if run.rows_written == 1 { "" } else { "s" });
   495	    respond(request, 200, json!({ "job": run.name, "id": run.id, "state": run.state, "chunks": run.chunks, "chunkSize": run.chunk_size, "retries": run.retries, "heapPeak": run.heap_peak, "rowsWritten": run.rows_written, "error": run.error }));
   496	}

   498	pub(super) fn clock_status(request: Request, shared: &Shared) {
   499	    if !shared.personas { return respond(request, 403, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&crate::dev_clock::release())})); }
   500	    let result = (|| {
   501	        let (epoch, reader) = shared.reader()?;
   502	        let note = crate::dev_clock_store::ahead(&reader, shared.now());
   503	        lock(&shared.readers).put(&epoch, reader.into_inner());
   504	        note
   505	    })();
   506	    match result {
   507	        Ok(note) => { let now = shared.now(); respond(request, 200, json!({"storeAhead":note,"now":now,"skewMs":now - snapback4_core::now_ms()})) },
   508	        Err(error) => respond(request, 500, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&error.refusal())})),
   509	    }
   510	}

//! The online-only mutation route and a wake state independent of the writer.
use super::*;
use snapback4_core::engine::ephemeral::{Hub, Snapshot};

pub(super) struct Wake {
    pub seq: u64,
    pub store_id: Option<String>,
    pub generation: u64,
    pub eph: Snapshot,
}
impl Wake {
    pub fn new(engine: &Engine) -> Self {
        Self {
            seq: engine.seq().unwrap_or(0),
            store_id: engine.store().meta("store_id").unwrap_or(None),
            generation: engine.generation(),
            eph: engine.ephemeral_hub().snapshot().expect("new hub"),
        }
    }
}
#[derive(Default)]
pub(super) struct Rate {
    buckets: Mutex<BTreeMap<String, (Instant, f64)>>,
    #[cfg(test)]
    fixed_now: Mutex<Option<Instant>>,
}
impl Rate {
    fn now(&self) -> Instant {
        #[cfg(test)]
        if let Some(now) = *lock(&self.fixed_now) {
            return now;
        }
        Instant::now()
    }
    #[cfg(test)]
    pub(super) fn set_now(&self, now: Instant) {
        *lock(&self.fixed_now) = Some(now);
    }
    pub fn admit(&self, key: String, now: Instant) -> bool {
        let mut buckets = lock(&self.buckets);
        buckets.retain(|_, (at, _)| now.saturating_duration_since(*at) < Duration::from_secs(60));
        if !buckets.contains_key(&key) && buckets.len() >= 4096 {
            return false;
        }
        let (at, tokens) = buckets.entry(key).or_insert((now, 40.0));
        *tokens = (*tokens + now.saturating_duration_since(*at).as_secs_f64() * 20.0).min(40.0);
        *at = now;
        if *tokens < 1.0 {
            false
        } else {
            *tokens -= 1.0;
            true
        }
    }
}
impl Shared {
    // @ref LLP 3000.017#3.3 — lock order engine → hub → wake.
    pub(super) fn install_ephemeral_wake(self: &Arc<Self>) {
        let owner = Arc::downgrade(self);
        self.ephemeral.set_publisher(move |snapshot| {
            if let Some(shared) = owner.upgrade() {
                let mut wake = lock(&shared.wake);
                wake.store_id = Some(snapshot.identity.clone());
                wake.generation = snapshot.generation;
                wake.eph = snapshot;
                drop(wake);
                shared.polls.notify_all();
            }
        }).expect("new hub publisher");
    }
    pub(super) fn durable_committed(&self, engine: &Engine) {
        self.publish_durable(engine, true);
    }
    pub(super) fn publish_engine(&self, engine: &Engine) {
        self.publish_durable(engine, false);
    }
    fn publish_durable(&self, engine: &Engine, committed: bool) {
        if let Ok(seq) = engine.seq() {
            let store_id = engine.store().meta("store_id").unwrap_or(None);
            let generation = engine.generation();
            let mut current = lock(&self.seq);
            let mut wake = lock(&self.wake);
            let changed = wake.seq != seq || wake.store_id != store_id || wake.generation != generation;
            *current = seq;
            wake.seq = seq;
            wake.store_id = store_id;
            wake.generation = generation;
            // The hub publisher alone owns wake.eph. Never wait for a running
            // ephemeral program while holding the serving engine here.
            if committed || changed {
                self.polls.notify_all();
                self.committed.notify_all();
            }
        }
    }
}

pub(super) fn failed(request: Request, shared: &Shared, id: Option<&str>, why: Refusal) {
    let wake = lock(&shared.wake);
    let (store_id, head) = (wake.store_id.clone(), wake.seq);
    drop(wake);
    respond_timed(
        request,
        shared,
        200,
        super::mutation_reply(json!({"state":"failed","id":id,"why":refusal_json(&why),"store_id":store_id,"head":head})),
    );
}

pub(super) fn serve(request: Request, shared: &Shared, op: &str, body: &str) {
    let payload = serde_json::from_str::<Json>(if body.is_empty() { "{}" } else { body });
    let id = payload
        .as_ref()
        .ok()
        .and_then(|p| p.get("id"))
        .and_then(Json::as_str)
        .map(str::to_owned);
    let failed = |request, why| failed(request, shared, id.as_deref(), why);
    let payload = match payload {
        Ok(p) => p,
        Err(e) => {
            return failed(
                request,
                Refusal::new(
                    "E_INPUT",
                    "input",
                    format!("the request body is not JSON: {e}"),
                ),
            );
        }
    };
    let principal = match principal_of(&request, shared) {
        Ok(p) => p.0,
        Err(e) => return failed(request, e),
    };
    // A name may have been durable in a previous generation. Receipt custody
    // precedes signature decoding, rate admission and ephemeral execution.
    // @ref LLP 3000.022#6 — a stored success never executes a replacement body.
    let fingerprint = match delivery_fingerprint(&payload) {
        Ok(value) => value,
        Err(why) => return failed(request, why),
    };
    {
        let mut engine = producing_engine(shared);
        let preflight = mutation_authority(&request, shared, &engine, &principal)
            .and_then(|()| intent_store(&engine, &payload))
            .and_then(|()| {
                let args = payload.get("args").cloned().unwrap_or(json!({}));
                id.as_deref().map(|id| engine.replay_mutation(&principal, id, op, &args))
                    .transpose().map(Option::flatten).map_err(|e| e.refusal())
            });
        match preflight {
            Ok(Some(out)) => {
                let (store_id, head) = match response_head(&mut engine) {
                    Ok(value) => value,
                    Err(why) => return respond_timed(request, shared, 503, json!({"denied":why})),
                };
                let mut reply = out.reply(id.as_deref());
                reply["store_id"] = json!(store_id);
                reply["head"] = json!(head);
                return respond_timed(request, shared, 200, reply);
            }
            Err(why) => return failed(request, why),
            Ok(None) => {
                if let Err(error)=engine.require_non_media_ephemeral(&principal,id.as_deref()) { return failed(request,error.refusal()); }
                // @ref LLP 3000#http-overload-diagnostics — an ID alone does not deduplicate ephemeral writes, including after schema adoption.
                if payload.get("retry_write").and_then(Json::as_bool) == Some(true) {
                    return failed(request, Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", "retry_write requires a durable mutation; refresh the operation signature"));
                }
                if let Err(error) = engine.schema().check_delivery(op, fingerprint.as_deref()) {
                    return failed(request, error.refusal());
                }
            }
        }
    }
    // Bearer digests identify sessions without retaining secrets. Dev personas
    // have no session token and each principal is their development session.
    let key = crate::auth::bearer_token(&request)
        .map(|token| snapback4_core::value::digest(&token))
        .unwrap_or_else(|_| format!("persona:{principal}"));
    if !shared.ephemeral_rate.admit(key, shared.ephemeral_rate.now()) {
        let mut why = Refusal::new(
            "E_RATE_LIMIT",
            "auth",
            "ephemeral writes allow 20 requests per second, burst 40; retry later",
        )
        .guide("ephemeral");
        why.retryable = true;
        return failed(request, why);
    }
    let signature = lock(&shared.bound)
        .programs
        .iter()
        .find(|p| p.program.name == op)
        .map(|p| p.program.args.clone());
    let Some(signature) = signature else {
        return failed(
            request,
            Refusal::new("E_OP", "op", format!("unknown operation {op}")),
        );
    };
    let empty = json!({});
    let args_json = payload.get("args").unwrap_or(&empty);
    if let Some(why)=super::dev_doors::persona_argument(shared,&signature,args_json) {return failed(request,why);}
    let Some(fields) = args_json.as_object() else {
        return failed(
            request,
            Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", "args must be an object"),
        );
    };

  1451	            let legacy_now = shared.now();

  1453	                let mut engine = producing_engine(shared);
  1454	                match service_of_locked(&request, shared, &engine) {
  1455	                    Err(refusal) => Err((401, refusal)),

  1466	                                .map_err(|error| (crate::auth::error_status(&error), error.refusal()))
  1467	                        }
  1468	                    },
  1469	                }
  1470	            };

  1472	                Ok(body) => respond_timed(request, shared, 200, body),

  1474	            }

  1480	            };

  1484	            };

  1488	            };

  1492	            }

  1497	        }

  1499	        (Method::Post, "/dev/reset") => dev_doors::reset(request, shared, &body),

  1501	    }
  1502	}
  1503

  1505	#[path = "../tests/serve_poison/mod.rs"]
    };
    let mut args = BTreeMap::new();
    for (name, value) in fields {
        let Some(kind) = signature.get(name) else {
            return failed(
                request,
                Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", format!("{op} takes no argument {name}")),
            );
        };
        match wire::from_json(kind, value) {
            Ok(value) => {
                args.insert(name.clone(), value);
            }
            Err(why) => {
                return failed(
                    request,
                    Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", format!("argument {name}: {why}")),
                );
            }
        }
    }

        let engine = producing_engine(shared);
        // @ref LLP 3000.019#3.6 — ephemeral writes also lose authority while queued for adoption.
        if let Err(why) = mutation_authority(&request, shared, &engine, &principal) {
            return failed(request, why);
        }
        (shared.take_reader(&engine), shared.personas.then(|| Arc::new(lock(&shared.bound).refusal_sites.clone())))
    };

        Ok((epoch, mut reader)) => {
            if let Some(sites) = sites { context = super::dev_refusals::response::context(context, sites, &reader); }
            let _timing = latency::EngineSpan::new();
            let result = intent_store(&reader, &payload).and_then(|()| {
                reader.require_non_media_ephemeral(&principal,id.as_deref()).map_err(|e|e.refusal())?;
                reader
                    .mutate_ephemeral(op, context)
                    .map_err(|e| snapback4_core::engine::seat_refusal(reader.schema(),&e,&principal))
            });
            let store_id = reader.store().meta("store_id").ok().flatten();
            if result.is_ok() {
                lock(&shared.readers).put(&epoch, reader);
            }
            result.map(|out| (out, store_id))
        }
        // In-memory test stores have no detached SQLite connection.
        Err(_) => {
            #[cfg(test)]
            test_work(&shared.mutation_wait);
            let mut engine = producing_engine(shared);
            if shared.personas { context = super::dev_refusals::response::context(context, Arc::new(lock(&shared.bound).refusal_sites.clone()), &engine); }
            mutation_authority(&request, shared, &engine, &principal)
                .and_then(|()| intent_store(&engine, &payload))
                .and_then(|()| {
                    engine.require_non_media_ephemeral(&principal,id.as_deref()).map_err(|e|e.refusal())?;
                    engine
                        .mutate_ephemeral(op, context)
                        .map_err(|e| snapback4_core::engine::seat_refusal(engine.schema(),&e,&principal))
                })
                .map(|out| (out, engine.store().meta("store_id").ok().flatten()))
        }
    };
    match result {
        Ok((out, store_id)) => {
            respond_timed(
                request,
                shared,
                200,
                super::mutation_reply(json!({"state":"sent","id":id,"result":wire::to_json(&out.result),"ephemeral":out.ephemeral,"store_id":store_id,"head":out.seq})),
            );
        }
        Err(why) => failed(request, why),
    }
}

pub(super) fn hub(engine: &Engine) -> Arc<Hub> {
    engine.ephemeral_hub()
}

/// Ordinary handwritten calls keep their spelling; SDK reports name the binding.
pub(super) fn delivery_fingerprint(payload: &Json) -> Result<Option<String>, Refusal> {
    let Some(delivery) = payload.get("delivery") else { return Ok(None) };
    delivery.get("fingerprint").and_then(Json::as_str).filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
        .map(|s| Some(s.to_owned())).ok_or_else(|| {
            let mut why = Refusal::new("E_DELIVERY_BINDING", "schema", "delivery needs the fingerprint collected from its binding").guide("receipts");
            why.site = Some("delivery.fingerprint".into());
            why.rewrite = Some("send delivery: { fingerprint } from the manifest or compiled binding".into());
            why
        })
}

//! The CLI's local service-seat door. This capability never comes from a bearer session.
use super::{Shared, single_header, authority_host, producing_engine, respond_with_cors};
use snapback4_core::{error::Refusal, identity::{self, Session}};
use std::{io::{self, Read, Seek, SeekFrom, Write}, net::TcpStream, path::{Path, PathBuf}, time::Duration};
use serde_json::{Value as Json, json};
use tiny_http::{Method, Request};

pub(crate) const ENDPOINT: &str = "/dev/token";
#[path = "serve_token_protocol.rs"]
mod protocol;
use protocol::{Mint, CLIENT, SERVER, PROOF};
pub(crate) use protocol::Authority;
const BODY_LIMIT: usize = 4096;
const SECRET_LEN: usize = 64;

fn secret_path(store: &Path) -> PathBuf {
    let mut path = store.as_os_str().to_owned();
    path.push("-token");
    path.into()
}

// @ref LLP 3000.019#3.4 — preserve the hardened auxiliary-file checks and the single owner's lifetime.
pub(crate) fn publish(store: &Path) -> io::Result<Authority> {
    #[cfg(unix)] {
        let secret = protocol::hex(&protocol::random()?);
        let mut file = snapback4_core::private_fs::auxiliary_file(store, &secret_path(store), true, SECRET_LEN as u64)?;
        file.set_len(0)?;
        file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(0))?;
        file.write_all(secret.as_bytes())?;
        Ok(Authority::new(secret, protocol::store_identity(store)?))
    }
    #[cfg(not(unix))] {
        let _ = store;
        Err(io::Error::other("local service minting requires Unix private files"))
    }
}

fn read_secret(store: &Path) -> io::Result<String> {
    #[cfg(unix)] {
        use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
        let file = snapback4_core::private_fs::auxiliary_file(store, &secret_path(store), false, SECRET_LEN as u64)?;
        if file.metadata()?.permissions().mode() & 0o777 != 0o600 {
            return Err(io::Error::other("the store token proof must have mode 0600"));
        }
        let mut secret = String::new();
        file.take((SECRET_LEN + 1) as u64).read_to_string(&mut secret)?;
        if secret.len() != SECRET_LEN || !secret.bytes().all(|c| c.is_ascii_hexdigit()) {
            return Err(io::Error::other("the store token proof is incomplete"));
        }
        Ok(secret)
    }
    #[cfg(not(unix))] {
        let _ = store;
        Err(io::Error::other("local service minting requires Unix private files"))
    }
}

fn refusal(code: &str, family: &str, message: &str, rewrite: &str) -> Refusal {
    Refusal::new(code, family, message).site(ENDPOINT).rewrite(rewrite).guide("services")
}

pub(super) fn denied(request: Request) {
    respond_with_cors(request, 403, json!({"denied": refusal("E_AUTH", "auth",
        "service token minting requires a loopback peer and this server's private store proof",
        "run snapback4 token --service <name> on the server host as the store owner (add --release <dir> for serve)")}), false);
}

// @ref LLP 3000.019#3.4 — authenticate both ends before minting; the store key never leaves its host file/memory.
pub(super) fn handle(mut request: Request, shared: &Shared) {
    let local = request.remote_addr().is_some_and(|peer| peer.ip().is_loopback())
        && matches!(single_header(&request, "host"), Ok(Some(host)) if authority_host(host)
            .is_some_and(|host| host.parse::<std::net::IpAddr>().is_ok_and(|ip| ip.is_loopback())))
        && matches!(single_header(&request, "origin"), Ok(None))
        && matches!(single_header(&request, "x-snapback-store-secret"), Ok(None));
    let Some(authority) = shared.owner.as_ref().and_then(|o| o.token_authority.as_ref()).filter(|_| local) else {
        return denied(request);
    };
    if request.method() != &Method::Post || request.url() != ENDPOINT
        || request.body_length().is_some_and(|n| n > BODY_LIMIT) { return denied(request); }
    let client = match single_header(&request, CLIENT) {
        Ok(Some(value)) => match protocol::nonce(value) { Some(nonce) => nonce, None => return denied(request) },
        _ => return denied(request),
    };
    let (server, proof) = match (single_header(&request, SERVER), single_header(&request, PROOF)) {
        (Ok(None), Ok(None)) => (None, None),
        (Ok(Some(server)), Ok(Some(proof))) => match protocol::nonce(server) {
            Some(server) => (Some(server), Some(proof.to_owned())), None => return denied(request),
        },
        _ => return denied(request),
    };
    let mut bytes = Vec::new();
    if request.as_reader().take((BODY_LIMIT + 1) as u64).read_to_end(&mut bytes).is_err() || bytes.len() > BODY_LIMIT {
        return denied(request);
    }
    let mint: Mint = match serde_json::from_slice::<Mint>(&bytes) {
        Ok(mint) if mint.store == authority.store => mint,
        _ => return denied(request),
    };
    let binding = mint.binding();
    let Some(server) = server else {
        let Some(server) = authority.challenge(client, binding.clone(), std::time::Instant::now()) else { return denied(request); };
        return respond_with_cors(request, 200, json!({"server_nonce": protocol::hex(&server),
            "server_proof": protocol::server_proof(&authority.secret, &client, &server, &binding)}), false);
    };
    if !authority.consume(&client, &server, &binding, proof.as_deref().unwrap(), std::time::Instant::now()) {
        return denied(request);
    }
    let result = {
        // Use the same writer and identity routine as offline minting. Sample
        // wall time as the offline CLI does, independent of dev's test clock.
        let engine = producing_engine(shared);
        shared.owner.as_ref().expect("authorized owner").path().and_then(|_| {
            identity::service_session(engine.store(), &mint.service, snapback4_core::now_ms(), mint.days)
        })
    };
    let reply = match result {
        Ok(session) => json!({"session": session}),
        Err(error) => {
            let why = error.refusal().site(ENDPOINT).rewrite(if matches!(error, snapback4_core::RuntimeError::Auth(_)) {
                "use --service with 1–64 letters, digits, _ or -"
            } else { "inspect the store error, repair the store access, then rerun snapback4 token" }).guide("services");
            json!({"denied": why})
        }
    };
    let Some(sealed) = protocol::seal(&authority.secret, &client, &server, &binding, &serde_json::to_vec(&reply).unwrap()) else {
        return denied(request);
    };
    respond_with_cors(request, 200, json!({"sealed": sealed}), false);
}

fn exchange(address: std::net::SocketAddr, headers: &str, body: &str) -> io::Result<Json> {
    let mut stream = TcpStream::connect_timeout(&address, Duration::from_secs(1))?;
    stream.set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(10)))?;
    stream.set_write_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(2)))?;
    // HTTP/1.0 keeps the bounded reply length-delimited. No proxy, DNS or redirects.
    write!(stream, "POST {ENDPOINT} HTTP/1.0\r\nHost: {address}\r\n{headers}Content-Type: application/json\r\nConnection: close\r\nContent-Length: {}\r\n\r\n{body}", body.len())?;
    let mut response = String::new();
    stream.take(8193).read_to_string(&mut response)?;
    response.split_once("\r\n\r\n").filter(|_| response.len() <= 8192
        && (response.starts_with("HTTP/1.0 200 ") || response.starts_with("HTTP/1.1 200 ")))
        .and_then(|(_, body)| serde_json::from_str(body).ok())
        .ok_or_else(|| io::Error::other("invalid local mint reply"))
}

// @ref LLP 3000.019#3.4 — busy token commands ask the announced loopback owner, never open a second writer.
pub(crate) fn mint_live(path: &Path, name: &str, days: i64) -> Result<Session, (i32, String)> {
    let store = path.canonicalize().unwrap_or_else(|_| path.to_owned());
    let owner = crate::store_owner::address(&store).unwrap_or_else(|| "another CLI command or a server starting up (address pending)".into());
    let unavailable = |reason: &str| (2, format!("E_STORE_BUSY at {}: owned by {owner}; {reason}. Restore access to that server's loopback listener and private store proof, then rerun `snapback4 token --service <name>` (with the same --release <dir> for serve). For an older or unreachable server, stop it, rerun token offline, then restart it; for another CLI, wait for it to finish. Leave <database>-owner in place", path.display()));
    let address = crate::store_owner::inspector_address(&store).ok_or_else(|| unavailable("no published loopback listener; no mint request sent"))?;
    let secret = read_secret(&store).map_err(|_| unavailable("cannot read the 0600 store token proof; no mint request sent"))?;
    let mint = Mint { service: name.into(), days, store: protocol::store_identity(&store)
        .map_err(|_| unavailable("cannot identify the owned store; no mint request sent"))? };
    let body = serde_json::to_string(&mint).unwrap();
    if body.len() > BODY_LIMIT { return Err((1, "token: E_AUTH at --service: a service name is 1–64 letters, digits, _ or -; use --service worker".into())); }
    let binding = mint.binding();
    let client = protocol::random().map_err(|_| unavailable("cannot create a fresh challenge; no mint request sent"))?;
    let headers = format!("{CLIENT}: {}\r\n", protocol::hex(&client));
    let challenge = exchange(address, &headers, &body).map_err(|_| unavailable("server challenge unavailable; no mint proof sent"))?;
    let server = challenge["server_nonce"].as_str().and_then(protocol::nonce)
        .ok_or_else(|| unavailable("invalid server challenge; no mint proof sent"))?;
    if !challenge["server_proof"].as_str().is_some_and(|proof| protocol::verify_server(&secret, &client, &server, &binding, proof)) {
        return Err(unavailable("server proof did not verify; no mint proof sent"));
    }
    // Only a verified server receives a client proof. Neither message contains the key.
    let headers = format!("{headers}{SERVER}: {}\r\n{PROOF}: {}\r\n", protocol::hex(&server),
        protocol::client_proof(&secret, &client, &server, &binding));
    let reply = exchange(address, &headers, &body)
        .map_err(|_| unavailable("mint reply unavailable; a session may have been minted, but no token was received"))?;
    let reply: Json = reply["sealed"].as_str().and_then(|sealed| protocol::open(&secret, &client, &server, &binding, sealed))
        .and_then(|bytes| serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).ok())
        .ok_or_else(|| unavailable("server returned an invalid mint reply; a session may have been minted"))?;
    if let Some(denied) = reply.get("denied") {
        if let Ok(why) = serde_json::from_value::<Refusal>(denied.clone()) {
            return Err((1, format!("token: {} at {ENDPOINT}: {}; {}", why.code, why.message, why.rewrite.unwrap_or_else(|| "rerun snapback4 token with valid service arguments".into()))));
        }
        return Err(unavailable("server refused the local mint request; restart it with this CLI and retry"));
    }
    let session = &reply["session"];
    let principal = format!("service:{name}");
    let token = session["token"].as_str().filter(|t| t.len() == 43 && t.bytes().all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b"_-".contains(&c)));
    if session["principal"] != principal || session["kind"] != "service" || token.is_none() || session["expires_at"].as_i64().is_none() {
        return Err(unavailable("server returned an invalid mint reply; a session may have been minted"));
    }
    Ok(Session { scope: snapback4_core::identity::SessionScope::Full, cap_expires_at: None, principal, kind: "service".into(), token: token.unwrap().into(), expires_at: session["expires_at"].as_i64().unwrap() })
}
//! HTTP identity admission. Password work owns a bounded KDF slot, never
//! the engine guard. Rate keys use the socket peer, never forwarded headers.
use crate::serve::{Shared, principal_of, refusal_json, respond_timed};
use serde_json::{Value as Json, json};
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
use snapback4_core::error::Refusal;
use snapback4_core::{RuntimeError, identity};
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::{
    Mutex,
    atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering},
};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};
use tiny_http::Request;

pub const BODY_CEILING: usize = 4096;
const WINDOW: Duration = Duration::from_secs(60);
const KEYS: usize = 4096;

pub struct Admission {
    attempts: Mutex<HashMap<String, (Instant, u32)>>,
    kdfs: AtomicUsize,
    dev_kdf_slots: usize,
}
impl Default for Admission {
    fn default() -> Self {
        // @ref LLP 3000.007#14 — ruling 9: dev loopback KDF work fits the host, bounded at 2–16 slots
        let dev_kdf_slots = std::thread::available_parallelism().map(|n| n.get().clamp(2, 16)).unwrap_or(2);
        Self { attempts: Mutex::new(HashMap::new()), kdfs: AtomicUsize::new(0), dev_kdf_slots }
    }
}
impl Admission {
    pub fn kdf_slots(&self, dev_loopback: bool) -> usize {
        if dev_loopback { self.dev_kdf_slots } else { 2 }
    }

    fn attempt(&self, peer: &str, email: Option<&str>, now: Instant) -> bool {
        let mut attempts = self.attempts.lock().unwrap();
        attempts.retain(|_, (start, _)| now.duration_since(*start) < WINDOW);
        let mut keys = vec![(format!("ip:{peer}"), 30)];
        if let Some(email) = email {
            keys.push((format!("email:{}", identity::normalized_email(email)), 10));
        }
        // Charge every attempt, including denials. A full table refuses new
        // keys until expiry rather than evicting a key under attack.
        let mut admitted = true;
        for (key, limit) in keys {
            // A peer that is already over budget may charge existing email
            // keys, but cannot fill the shared map by rotating fresh emails.
            if !admitted && !attempts.contains_key(&key) {
                continue;
            }
            if !attempts.contains_key(&key) && attempts.len() >= KEYS {
                admitted = false;
                continue;
            }
            let (_, count) = attempts.entry(key).or_insert((now, 0));
            *count = count.saturating_add(1);
            admitted &= *count <= limit;
        }
        admitted
    }
    fn kdf(&self, dev_loopback: bool) -> Option<Kdf<'_>> {
        let slots = self.kdf_slots(dev_loopback);
        self.kdfs
            .fetch_update(Ordering::AcqRel, Ordering::Acquire, |n| {
                (n < slots).then_some(n + 1)
            })
            .ok()?;
        Some(Kdf(&self.kdfs))
    }
}
struct Kdf<'a>(&'a AtomicUsize);
impl Drop for Kdf<'_> {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.0.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::Release);
    }
}
fn limited(request: Request, shared: &Shared) {
    let mut refusal = Refusal::new(
        "E_RATE_LIMIT",
        "auth",
        "too many identity requests; retry later",
    )
    .guide("personas");
    refusal.retryable = true;
    respond_timed(request, shared, 429, json!({ "denied": refusal_json(&refusal) }));
}

pub fn handle(request: Request, shared: &Shared, path: &str, body: &str) {
    let payload: Json = match serde_json::from_str(if body.is_empty() { "{}" } else { body }) {
        Ok(value) => value,
        Err(_) => {
            return respond_timed(request, shared,
                400,
                json!({ "denied": Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", "identity takes a JSON object") }),
            );
        }
    };
    let email = payload.get("email").and_then(Json::as_str).unwrap_or("");
    let password = payload.get("password").and_then(Json::as_str).unwrap_or("");
    let password_route = matches!(path, "/auth/login" | "/auth/signup");
    let peer = request
        .remote_addr()
        .map(|a| a.ip().to_string())
        .unwrap_or_else(|| "unknown".into());
    let rate_route = matches!(path, "/auth/login" | "/auth/signup" | "/auth/guest");
    // @ref LLP 3000.007#8 — dev loopback has no minute counters; KDF slots remain
    let dev_loopback = shared.personas && request.remote_addr().is_some_and(|peer| peer.ip().is_loopback());
    if rate_route && !dev_loopback
        && !shared
            .auth
            .attempt(&peer, password_route.then_some(email), Instant::now())
    {
        return limited(request, shared);
    }
    let kdf = if password_route {
        match shared.auth.kdf(dev_loopback) {
            Some(permit) => Some(permit),
            None => return limited(request, shared),
        }
    } else {
        None
    };
    let scope = match payload.get("scope") {
        None => Ok(identity::SessionScope::Full),
        Some(Json::String(value)) if value == "full" => Ok(identity::SessionScope::Full),
        Some(Json::String(value)) if value == "read" => Ok(identity::SessionScope::Read),
        _ => Err(RuntimeError::Input("scope must be full or read".into())),
    };
    let outcome = scope.and_then(|scope| perform(&request, shared, path, email, password, scope));
    drop(kdf);
    match outcome {
        Ok(Outcome::Refused(why)) => respond_refused(request, shared, why),
        Ok(Outcome::SupervisedRefresh) => respond_timed(request, shared, 403, json!({ "denied": refusal_json(&Refusal::new(
            "E_WORKER_REFRESH", "auth", "supervised worker tokens are rotated by the supervisor; keep using the injected token",
        ).guide("effects")) })),
        Ok(Outcome::Logout) => respond_timed(request, shared, 200, json!({ "ok": true })),
        Ok(Outcome::LogoutAll(revoked)) => {
            respond_timed(request, shared, 200, json!({ "ok": true, "revoked": revoked }))
        }
        Ok(Outcome::Session(session)) => {
            let mut wire = json!({ "principal": session.principal, "kind": session.kind, "token": session.token, "expiresAt": session.expires_at, "scope": session.scope });
            if let Some(cap) = session.cap_expires_at { wire["capExpiresAt"] = json!(cap); }
            respond_timed(request, shared, 200, json!({ "session": wire }));
        },
        Err(error) => {
            if matches!(path, "/auth/logout" | "/auth/narrow" | "/auth/refresh" | "/auth/logout-all")
                && let RuntimeError::Auth(message) = &error {
                return respond_refused(request, shared, Refusal::new("E_AUTH", "auth", message).guide("personas"));
            }
            let status = error_status(&error);
            respond_timed(request, shared, status, json!({ "denied": refusal_json(&error.refusal()) }));
        }
    }
}

enum Outcome {
    Refused(Refusal),
    Session(identity::Session),
    SupervisedRefresh,
    Logout,
    LogoutAll(u64),
}

pub(crate) fn error_status(error: &RuntimeError) -> u16 {
    if matches!(error, RuntimeError::Auth(_)) { 401 }
    else if error.is_refusal() { 200 } else { 503 }
}

// @ref LLP 3000.007#20.2 — identity operations preserve the same refusal envelope as data doors.
fn respond_refused(request: Request, shared: &Shared, why: Refusal) {
    respond_timed(request, shared, if why.retryable { 503 } else { 401 }, json!({ "denied": refusal_json(&why) }));
}

fn refused_bearer(request: &Request, shared: &Shared, engine: &snapback4_core::Engine, token: &str) -> Outcome {
    Outcome::Refused(identity::diagnostics::refused(engine.store(), token, shared.now(), crate::serve::trusted_dev_request(request, shared)))
}

/// Translate only after the identity operation's own transactional check failed.
/// A still-live but wrong-kind credential keeps its endpoint-specific explanation.
fn credential_result(request: &Request, shared: &Shared, engine: &snapback4_core::Engine, token: &str,
    result: Result<Outcome, RuntimeError>) -> Result<Outcome, RuntimeError> {
    match result {
        Err(RuntimeError::Auth(message)) => {
            let sample = identity::ServiceSample { now: shared.now(), supervisor_revision: shared.worker_revision.load(Ordering::Acquire) };
            if identity::resolve_supervised(engine.store(), token, sample)?.is_none() {
                Ok(refused_bearer(request, shared, engine, token))
            } else { Ok(Outcome::Refused(Refusal::new("E_AUTH", "auth", message).guide("personas"))) }
        }
        result => result,
    }
}

// RFC 7235: the authentication scheme is case-insensitive. Accept HTTP
// whitespace consistently at every entry, including detached poll rechecks.
pub(crate) fn parse_bearer(value: &str) -> Option<&str> {
    let mut words = value.split_ascii_whitespace();
    let scheme = words.next()?;
    let token = words.next()?;
    (scheme.eq_ignore_ascii_case("Bearer") && words.next().is_none()).then_some(token)
}

pub(crate) fn bearer_token(request: &Request) -> Result<&str, RuntimeError> {
    let mut headers = request
        .headers()
        .iter()
        .filter(|header| header.field.equiv("authorization"));
    let value = headers.next().ok_or_else(|| {
        RuntimeError::Auth("this identity operation needs the bearer token".into())
    })?;
    if headers.next().is_some() {
        return Err(RuntimeError::Auth(
            "send exactly one Authorization header".into(),
        ));
    }
    parse_bearer(value.value.as_str())
        .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Auth("send Authorization: Bearer <token>".into()))
}

//! Advice is evidence about known template bytes, or explicitly a heuristic.
// @ref LLP 3000.011.003.000.000#11-wave-14-truthful-starter-custody-day4 — custom proofs own their arguments and assertions.
use std::path::Path;
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
use serde::Deserialize;

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct Template { file: String, version: String, template: Option<String>, web: bool, sha256: String }
fn templates() -> &'static [Template] {
    static TEMPLATES: std::sync::OnceLock<Vec<Template>> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    TEMPLATES.get_or_init(|| serde_json::from_str(include_str!("proof-digests.json")).expect("shipped proof digests"))
}
fn digest(text: &str) -> String { format!("{:x}", Sha256::digest(text.as_bytes())) }
pub(super) fn known_day2(text: &str) -> bool {
    let hash = digest(text);
    templates().iter().any(|t| t.file == "day2" && t.sha256 == hash)
}
pub(super) fn frontend_template(dir: &Path, web: bool) -> Option<(&'static str, Option<&'static str>)> {
    let text = std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("scripts/frontend-proof.mjs")).ok()?;
    let hash = digest(&text);
    templates().iter().find(|t| t.file == "frontend" && t.web == web && t.sha256 == hash)
        .map(|t| (t.version.as_str(), t.template.as_deref()))
}
pub(super) fn known_frontend(dir: &Path) -> bool { [false,true].into_iter().any(|web|frontend_template(dir,web).is_some()) }
fn package(dir: &Path) -> serde_json::Value {
    std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("package.json")).ok().and_then(|s|serde_json::from_str(&s).ok()).unwrap_or_default()
}
pub(super) fn referenced(dir: &Path, path: &str) -> bool {
    package(dir)["scripts"].as_object().is_some_and(|scripts| scripts.values().any(|v|v.as_str().is_some_and(|s|s.contains(path))))
}
pub(super) fn report(dir: &Path) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut advice = Vec::new();
    for path in ["scripts/frontend-proof.mjs", "scripts/day2-proof.mjs", "scripts/launch.mjs"] {
        if !dir.join(path).exists() && referenced(dir, path) {
            advice.push(format!("info: {path} is missing but package.json still references it; preview `snapback4 init --adapt`, then `snapback4 init --adapt --apply`"));
        }
    }
    if let Ok(text) = std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("scripts/day2-proof.mjs")) {
        let hash=digest(&text);
        if let Some(t)=templates().iter().find(|t| t.file=="day2" && t.sha256==hash) {
            if matches!(t.version.as_str(),"0.4.28"|"0.4.29") {
                advice.push(format!("info: scripts/day2-proof.mjs is the unmodified {} starter: it asserts no business rows; preview `snapback4 init --adapt` to replace it and capture current sources/fixtures",t.version));
            }
            if t.version=="0.4.30" || t.version=="0.4.31" {
                let script=package(dir)["scripts"]["day2:proof"].as_str().unwrap_or("").to_owned();
                if script=="node scripts/day2-proof.mjs" {
                    advice.push("info: the unmodified day-two starter needs its two saved-source arguments; preview `snapback4 init --adapt`".into());
                }
            }
        }
    }
    if let Ok(text)=std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("scripts/frontend-proof.mjs")) {
        // Custom JavaScript can hide builds in arbitrary imports/functions. These
        // checks deliberately make no claim about its behavior or ownership.
        let active=text.lines().filter(|line| !line.trim_start().starts_with("//")).collect::<Vec<_>>().join("\n");
        let flat=active.replace(['\"','\'',',','[',']','(',')'], " ");
        let words=flat.split_whitespace().collect::<Vec<_>>();
        let serves_dist=words.windows(2).any(|w|w==["startStatic","dist"]);
        let pkg=package(dir);
        let launch=pkg["scripts"]["frontend:proof"].as_str().unwrap_or("");
        let pre=pkg["scripts"]["prefrontend:proof"].as_str().unwrap_or("");
        let builds=|s:&str|s.contains("build")||s.contains("export");
        if serves_dist && !builds(&active) && !builds(launch) && !builds(pre) {
            advice.push("info: scripts/frontend-proof.mjs serves dist with no visible build step (heuristic; imported code may build it); build in the proof or its npm script before startStatic(\"dist\")".into());
        }
        if words.windows(3).any(|w|w==["npx","snapback4","dev"]) {
            advice.push("info: scripts/frontend-proof.mjs launches npx snapback4 dev (heuristic); use startDev from snapback4/proof for an owned server and bounded cleanup".into());
        }
    }
    advice
}

# Rules

**Snapback 2 optimizes the edit-to-verified loop — the agent's building an app on it, and ours building it.**

Speed is the constraint. Everything below exists to keep the edit-to-verified loop short
and to stop this repository accreting apparatus faster than anyone can remove it. These
rules bind `snapback2/` and the LLPs numbered 1000 and up; Snapback 1 is baselined, not
exempt, and its numbers may only fall.

Each rule is **[check]** (enforced by `caps`) or **[review]** (enforced by a human).

## Budgets — every budget is a trade, not a limit

- **5 blocking checks, 60s total.** A sixth requires deleting one, in the same PR. **[check]**
- **59 documents in the working set** (`llp/current/`). Today's count. A 60th requires
  archiving one — which is just removing the link. Snapback 2 aims to leave this at 15;
  Snapback 1's links are archived at promotion. **[check]**
- **12 documents in the foundation** (`llp/foundation/`). **[check]**
- **This file: 700 words.** If it grows, something becomes a check or stops being a rule. **[check]**
- **1,500 lines per source file, baseline 204.** Generated files exempt — and generated
  files are built, not committed; so are benchmark run records under `benchmarks/runs/`,
  which are evidence, not source. The baseline is Snapback 1's oversize count on the day
  the rule landed; it may not grow, and `snapback2/` contributes zero to it. **[check]**

## Blocking checks

`caps` · `ref-check` · `snapback2/scripts/test.sh` · `snapback2/scripts/measure.mjs --check` · `check-inventories`

## Loop shape

- **Every check reports all failures in one run.** Fail-fast is banned. **[check]**
- **Nothing blocks on anything slower than 60 seconds.** Slow verification runs on a
  schedule, attributed to the breaking commit, and files a bounded set of issues. **[review]**
- **Fix loops get 3 rounds.** Then stop: escalate to a human or descope. **[review]**

## Time budgets

Tracked every run of `snapback2/scripts/measure.mjs` (appends `snapback2/metrics/loop.jsonl`).
A regression is a P0 with a name on it.

| | budget |
|---|---|
| Incremental rebuild after a one-line edit | 15s |
| Test what you just changed | 30s |
| Blocking gate suite | 60s |
| Full build, warm cache | 5 min |
| **`snapback2 check` on a program (the agent's product latency)** | **1s** |
| **`snapback2 doctor` boot-to-ready** | **0.5s** |

## Scope

- **`NOT-DOING.md` is binding.** Moving something onto the doing-list means writing why
  and taking something off. **[review]**
- **Delete; don't deprecate.** No compat shims or migration paths before promotion. **[review]**
- **Nothing is compiled, transpiled, or generated at runtime that could be built ahead of
  time.** **[review]**
- **A spec needs an implementer and a date, or it isn't written.** **[review]**
- **Only implemented specs bind.** A document with no running code behind it is a
  proposal, and a proposal cannot block a PR or justify a check. **[review]**

## Agents

- **Agents remove apparatus freely and add none.** An agent PR that adds a check, script,
  registry, config file, or design doc needs explicit human approval saying so. **[review]**
- **2026-09-06 session exception:** the user delegated the search implementation
  decisions; one `snapback2-core/build.rs` may generate pinned Unicode tables at
  build time, alongside the existing package build. No new gate, registry,
  runtime generator, or Unicode dependency is authorized by this exception. **[review]**
- **Snapback 2 LLPs are numbered 1000 and up**; `llp-create` must be told. **[review]**
- **Snapback 4 LLPs are numbered 3000 and up** (`snapback4/`, LLP 3000); it adopts these budgets
  and loop shape as its own and keeps its scope in `snapback4/NOT-DOING.md`. **[review]**

## Shared machines

- Warm, named lanes, one per stream of work. Never clone fresh; reuse the worktree.
- **Never `git stash`.** Use a temporary commit.
- Kill only PIDs you recorded at launch. Never by name or pattern.
certifying **authorization and shape** and stop pricing **bytes and steps**,
which move to a deterministic runtime meter with honest `capped`/abort
outcomes; and (2) the client should hold **a replica of the viewer's declared
partition** — the local-first shape every shipped sync engine and Snapback
2's own `deliver` log converge on — instead of a per-query result cache
proven by receipts. Those two flips dissolve most of the machinery that
leaked into the application (receipts, coverage, halos, validators, grants,
ID slices, drains, `withHistory`, follower inboxes, per-table retention

the device's write speed. The first slice should be built on the **hub
